questions.prompt: What does a density matrix describe that a simple state vector cannot?
options: Mixed states (statistical uncertainty), in addition to pure states
questions.explanation: Density matrices can represent mixed states — statistical uncertainty about the state itself — unlike a simple state vector which only describes pure states.

questions.prompt: What does the no-cloning theorem prove?
options: Quantum states can always be perfectly copied
It's impossible to create an identical copy of an arbitrary unknown quantum state
questions.explanation: The no-cloning theorem proves that an arbitrary unknown quantum state cannot be perfectly copied — a foundational result with security implications.

questions.prompt: How does measuring one qubit in an entangled pair affect the other?
options: It has no effect on the other qubit
It instantly affects the correlated state of the other qubit
It only affects qubits in the same physical location
questions.explanation: Due to entanglement, measuring one qubit instantly determines correlated information about the other, regardless of distance.

questions.prompt: What formal object generalizes projective measurement to describe imperfect real measurement devices?
questions.explanation: A POVM generalizes measurement theory to accurately model real, imperfect measurement devices.

questions.prompt: How many real parameters does a general pure state of n qubits need (after normalisation and global phase)?
